descriptors.R: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1921 to 1933
descriptors.D: nominee of the party in office since 1933, renominating the sitting President

compile_desc.R: the party that held the presidency from 1921 to 1933

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including a Union party, a Socialist and a Communist nominee (answer "other").
never_name: Landon, Roosevelt, Knox, Garner, Lemke, Norman Thomas, Browder, Coughlin, Townsend, Huey Long or Hoover

slice_sources.men: 1930 and 1940 censuses interpolated to November 1936 (the 1930 "Mexican" race category folded back into white, as the 1940 census recoded it); men 21+ outside the eleven Southern states, citizens only, American Indians included as citizens since 1924; Black voters here, mostly in Northern cities, swing toward the Democrats from 1936; calibrated to certified 1936 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1936, women 21+ outside the South, all enfranchised by the Nineteenth Amendment; turnout from the carried-forward women-to-men ratio, calibrated to each state's 1936 vote.
slice_sources.south-white: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1936, white adults (including Mexican-origin adults, listed separately in 1930) in the eleven former Confederate states; poll taxes remain in most (Louisiana repealed its in 1934); calibrated to certified 1936 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1936, Black adults in the eleven former Confederate states; disfranchisement by poll tax, literacy test and the white primary continues, so the shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion; the few who vote share in the Black realignment toward the Democrats that begins in 1936.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1930–1940 interpolation to November 1936, foreign-born white adults who were not naturalized; no state let aliens vote.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
